ART.01.note: Smarthistory reconstructs Brunelleschi's demonstration and Alberti's later codification, showing linear perspective as a geometric viewing system rather than a general measure of realism.

exercise.prompt: Construct a one-point-perspective room with horizon line, station point, vanishing point, orthogonals and repeated floor tiles that diminish consistently.

ART.02.note: The Met connects nineteenth-century colour science to Neo-Impressionist experiments in simultaneous contrast, optical mixture, divisionism and pointillism.

exercise.prompt: Place identical grey swatches on different coloured grounds, record the apparent changes, and build a small image using optical rather than palette mixing.

ART.03.note: The National Gallery defines chiaroscuro through modelling with light and dark, while Smarthistory separates the more extreme theatrical darkness of tenebrism.

exercise.prompt: Light one object from a single side and make two studies: one using gradual chiaroscuro modelling and another using a tenebrist jump from darkness to illumination.

ART.04.note: The Met's technical study of Thomas Cole shows how microscopy, X-radiography, infrared imaging and pigment analysis reveal both ancient and newly industrialised colours in one artist's practice.

article.title: Modern Pigments Found in Thomas Cole's Paintings Shed New Light on the Artist's Practice

exercise.prompt: Build a pigment timeline for natural ultramarine, Prussian blue, synthetic ultramarine, chrome yellow and modern organic pigments, including cost, chemistry and conservation risks.

ART.05.note: The Met traces how Japanese prints altered European cropping, flattened space, colour, everyday subject matter and asymmetrical composition rather than merely supplying exotic motifs.

exercise.prompt: Compare one ukiyo-e print with one European Japoniste work and mark borrowed choices in cropping, viewpoint, contour, pattern, depth and subject matter.

ART.06.note: MoMA presents the Bauhaus as an experimental school joining fine art, craft, industry, architecture and social ideas across its Weimar, Dessau and Berlin phases.

exercise.prompt: Redesign one household object using a Bauhaus-style brief that balances function, manufacture, materials, geometry, affordability and visual clarity.

ART.07.note: MoMA's New Typography exhibition places hierarchy, asymmetry, sans-serif type, photography and information design within the Central European avant-garde and Bauhaus context.

exercise.prompt: Typeset the same short announcement three ways, changing family, weight, size, measure, leading, kerning and hierarchy while keeping the words identical.

ART.08.note: Getty's formal-analysis guide treats composition through line, shape, value, balance, emphasis, movement and the active relationship between positive and negative space.

exercise.prompt: Reduce one image to black positive shapes and white negative shapes, then move one element at a time and record changes in balance, tension, direction and emphasis.

ART.09.note: The House of European History places Van Meegeren within a wider history of counterfeiting, provenance, expert judgement and scientific authentication rather than celebrating him as a folk hero.

exercise.prompt: Design an authentication plan using provenance, stylistic comparison, support dating, imaging, pigment and binder analysis, and explain why no single test proves authorship.

ART.10.note: The National Gallery explains preventive care, examination, scientific analysis, cleaning and restoration as documented, approved interventions constrained by material evidence and reversibility concerns.

exercise.prompt: Write a treatment proposal distinguishing original material, ageing, dirt, varnish, old restoration and loss, then justify what should be preserved, removed, stabilised or visually reintegrated.

ART.11.note: The National Gallery of Art connects Impressionism's outdoor practice to portable tube paints and rail travel while also emphasizing modern life, light, brushwork and exhibition culture.

article.title: What Is Impressionism? 4 Things to Know

exercise.prompt: Paint or photograph the same outdoor scene at three times of day and identify how portability, speed, changing light and modern pigments alter the working method.

ART.12.note: MoMA's account of Duchamp's readymades shows that modern art did not simply abandon realism after photography; artists challenged medium, authorship, skill, beauty and the institutional definition of art.

exercise.prompt: Choose an ordinary object and argue for or against its presentation as art using selection, context, intention, craft, originality, audience and institutional framing.
